summary: Iteration 2 — tested the 4 new features (Savings Goals, Recurring Expenses, Best Bot of the Month badge, Export CSV) plus regression. Backend: 5 new pytest tests + 11 regression tests all green (16/16). Frontend: goals full CRUD with progress bar + goal money isolation from general balance (verified in UI: general 'Current Balance' unchanged after +300/−100 to a goal), recurring expenses card creates + materializes into ledger + pause toggle + delete all work, exactly one 'Best this month' badge shown on Bots page, Compare chart toggle works, and both Export CSV and Export JSON buttons trigger downloads with correct filenames.
critical_code_review_comments: server.py has grown to ~990 lines — still readable but nearing the 'split into modules' threshold; recurring/goal helpers are good candidates to extract.
GET /api/savings filters {goal_id: None} which correctly matches both null and missing fields in MongoDB — verified by isolation test.
Route ordering is correct: /savings/goals and /expenses/recurring declared before /savings/{tx_id} and /expenses/{item_id} respectively.

delete_profile purges bots/funds/etc. but does NOT purge new collections savings_goals / recurring_expense / recurring_income — orphaned rows remain in DB after profile deletion (pre-existing pattern; low-risk since profile_id is scoped anyway, but worth cleaning up).
_materialize_recurring_expenses and _materialize_recurring share nearly identical logic — could be DRY'd into one helper parametrised by collection.
test_credentials: Passwordless — GET /api/profiles → POST /api/auth/select with the 'Alex Demo' profile id.
seed_data_creation: Ephemeral TEST_-prefixed profile (isolated), TEST_ goals/recurring/bots — all cleaned up after tests.
context_for_next_testing_agent: Frontend routes use /cashflow (no dash) and /savings. Best-badge testid pattern: best-badge-<botId>. Recurring expense category is a shadcn Select — click the trigger, wait 400ms, then click 'div[role=option]:has-text("<Category>")' with force=True. Downloads captured via page.expect_download. All 16 backend pytest tests remain green; both test files are safe to reuse as regression.
